The minimum $a$ and maximum $b$ of such a subset must satisfy $a + b = 13$. A singleton would need $a = b$, which would give $2a = 13$, impossible, so $a < b$.

Since $a + b = 13$ with $1 \le a < b \le 12$, the valid pairs are $(a,b) = (1,12), (2,11), (3,10), (4,9), (5,8), (6,7)$.

For a pair $(a,b)$, a subset with minimum $a$ and maximum $b$ must contain both $a$ and $b$. Each of the $b-a-1$ integers strictly between them can be included or excluded freely. So there are $2^{b-a-1}$ such subsets. Since $b - a = 13 - 2a$:

| $(a,b)$ | $b-a-1$ | Count |
|---|---|---|
| (1,12) | 10 | 1024 |
| (2,11) | 8 | 256 |
| (3,10) | 6 | 64 |
| (4,9) | 4 | 16 |
| (5,8) | 2 | 4 |
| (6,7) | 0 | 1 |

Total: $1024 + 256 + 64 + 16 + 4 + 1 = 1365$.

ANSWER: 1365
